Emma — thanks for the clear list and the DPIA spreadsheet. Quick acknowledgement and summary here; we'll send a short written Q&A and attach the subprocessor inventory and our DPA redlines. For full technical evidence we can also provide a region-by-request trace sample under NDA.

High level answers (summary):
- Primary execution regions we operate today: US (us-east-1, us-west-2), EU (eu-west-1), APAC (ap-southeast-1). We deploy model serving in those regions and prefer routing to the nearest available region for latency.
- Subprocessors that may process plaintext payloads: our core cloud providers (AWS managed ML infra), select edge caching partners, and our telemetry vendor for observability. We'll attach the current signed subprocessor list.
- Failover behavior: requests prefer the origin region; on capacity or regional outage we fail over to the nearest compatible region (typical order: same region -> neighboring region in same geography -> primary US region). Transient in-flight data is ephemeral; we persist minimal request metadata for debugging (request_id, timestamp, model version) and only keep full request payloads transiently for up to 24 hours unless retention is requested for evals.
- Deletion SLA: standard commit is erasure of transient request payloads within 30 days and removal from KV/prefix caches within 72 hours. Backups are covered by our backup retention policy (up to 90 days) and included in the DPA; we can offer a shorter backup-window for enterprise customers as an add-on.
- Telemetry/logging: aggregated telemetry may be routed to the US for processing; PII is redacted from logs by default. We'll provide field-level mapping in the subprocessor PDF.

Next steps: I'll loop in our security team and send the subprocessor inventory + DPA redlines attached. If you want, we can schedule a quick 30-min technical walkthrough tomorrow.

Best,
Markus Klein

Emma — thanks for the patience. Below is the formal Q&A that you can include in your packet. I've attached the up-to-date subprocessor inventory (PDF) and our DPA redline for your legal team. If you need signed attestations or a sample trace, we can generate those under NDA.

Q1 — Where are requests executed?
Answer: We operate production serving in these primary regions today: US (us-east-1, us-west-2), EU (eu-west-1), APAC (ap-southeast-1). Requests are routed by latency and policy; customers can pin region preferences for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Q2 — Failover / cross-border processing behavior
Answer: Normal behavior is to process in the originating region. On regional capacity or outage, requests can fail over to the nearest compatible region. For EU-originating requests, failover occurs to EU-first peers, then to US as last resort. Any transient cross-border processing is ephemeral — full request payloads are kept transiently (default max 24 hours) for debugging unless otherwise configured. We retain minimal request metadata for 180 days for operational tracing; PII is redacted from these traces by default.

Q3 — Deletion timelines and scope
Answer: Standard erasure commitments: 
- Transient request payloads: removed within 30 days from request or immediately upon customer-initiated deletion.
- KV/prefix caches: evicted within 72 hours after eviction request.
- Backups/snapshots: default retention up to 90 days; we offer an enterprise option to contractually reduce backup retention to 45 days.
Notes: We can provide deletion certificates for compliance upon completion of the erase operation; evidence packages are available under SOC2/enterprise SLA.

Q4 — Telemetry and logging transfers
Answer: Aggregated telemetry and observability pipelines may consolidate in our US processing stack. Logs are sanitized — PII fields are masked or redacted. The attached subprocessor PDF enumerates vendors and field-level flows.

Q5 — Subprocessor list and controls
Answer: Attached is the latest subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_list_20280209.pdf). All subprocessors operate under contractually required security and data processing terms; we update customers on changes per the DPA notification schedule.

Attachments: subprocessor_list_20280209.pdf, redline_DPA_AtlasMed.docx

Next steps: If AtlasMed wants an expedited erase SLA (7 days) or a shorter backup window, we can add that as a contract add-on and reflect it in the DPA. Happy to set a short technical call to walk through the subprocessor list and show a sample (redacted) trace.
